classifications.definition: No accepted exposure or approved entry exists; investment outcome attribution is unavailable.
The selected issuer or security was inferior to available alternatives after comparable evidence and mandate constraints.
The original operating, accounting, competitive or governance thesis was materially wrong or incomplete.
The company thesis may be intact, but the entry price or assumed multiple failed to preserve the required risk/reward.
The thesis horizon or catalyst timing was wrong despite an otherwise valid company and valuation case.
Exposure magnitude was inconsistent with evidence quality, downside, liquidity or portfolio concentration.
Stale, incomplete, inconsistent or incorrectly mapped data drove the conclusion.
Order, fee, liquidity, operational or implementation effects impaired the result independently of thesis quality.
A material external event outside the underwritten range dominated the outcome.
The position or recommendation persisted after the original thesis, catalysts or kill conditions changed.
